normalization: Borda 5..1 per ballot; each model's points divided by its number of valid ballots in the field, summed over models (max 15)

candidates.motivation: for developing structural methods for the empirical analysis of demand and market power in differentiated-product markets

defining_works.work: Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes, 1995: Automobile Prices in Market Equilibrium, Econometrica
Berry, 1994: Estimating Discrete-Choice Models of Product Differentiation, RAND Journal of Economics
Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes, 2004: Differentiated Products Demand Systems from a Combination of Micro and Macro Data, Journal of Political Economy
Olley and Pakes, 1996: The Dynamics of Productivity in the Telecommunications Equipment Industry, Econometrica

candidates.reasoning: BLP is described as the workhorse of empirical IO, used daily in merger review and antitrust worldwide, combining equilibrium modelling with estimation and with clear attribution. The recurring reservation is sensitivity to instruments, conduct and computational assumptions, and closeness to econometrics.
candidates.grouping_note: Joins all BLP nominations, including several that name only Berry and Pakes and some that also mention Olley-Pakes or Ericson-Pakes dynamics, which have separate candidates of their own.

candidates.motivation: for measuring management practices and their effects on productivity across firms and countries

defining_works.work: Bloom and Van Reenen, 2007: Measuring and Explaining Management Practices Across Firms and Countries, Quarterly Journal of Economics
Bloom, Eifert, Mahajan, McKenzie and Roberts, 2013: Does Management Matter? Evidence from India, Quarterly Journal of Economics
Bloom, Sadun and Van Reenen, 2012: Americans Do IT Better: US Multinationals and the Productivity Miracle, American Economic Review

candidates.reasoning: The World Management Survey created durable measurement infrastructure, backed by a field experiment, linking management to productivity dispersion. The main reservations are the youth of the candidates, survey-based measurement and limited causal settings.
candidates.grouping_note: Most nominations name Bloom and Van Reenen only; Sadun is added in several.

candidates.motivation: for the analysis of endogenous sunk costs and the bounds approach to market structure

defining_works.work: Sutton, 1991: Sunk Costs and Market Structure, MIT Press
Sutton, 1998: Technology and Market Structure, MIT Press
Sutton, 2007: Market Structure: Theory and Evidence, in Handbook of Industrial Organization

candidates.reasoning: Sutton derived robust bounds on concentration that hold across game forms and explained why concentration need not fall as markets grow, linking theory to cross-industry evidence. The main reservation is that his influence on current empirical and policy practice is smaller than that of structural IO.
candidates.grouping_note: Joins all single-name Sutton nominations; joint nominations with Bresnahan and Reiss are placed in the entry candidate.

candidates.motivation: for the theory of two-sided markets and platform competition

people_others.name: David S. Evans
people_others.affiliation: Global Economics Group and University College London

defining_works.work: Rochet and Tirole, 2003: Platform Competition in Two-Sided Markets, Journal of the European Economic Association
Armstrong, 2006: Competition in Two-Sided Markets, RAND Journal of Economics
Caillaud and Jullien, 2003: Chicken and Egg: Competition among Intermediation Service Providers, RAND Journal of Economics
Rochet and Tirole, 2006: Two-Sided Markets: A Progress Report, RAND Journal of Economics

candidates.reasoning: Platform theory is seen as central to digital markets, payments and competition policy. The main reservation is overlap with Tirole's 2014 prize and limited empirical validation.
candidates.grouping_note: Third names vary (Jullien, Evans, Parker); David S. Evans and Geoffrey G. Parker are left out, and Tirole, a prior laureate, is not named.

candidates.motivation: for the empirical analysis of productivity dispersion, firm dynamics and reallocation using microdata

people_others.name: Steven J. Davis
people_others.affiliation: University of Chicago Booth School of Business and Hoover Institution

defining_works.work: Foster, Haltiwanger and Krizan, 2001: Aggregate Productivity Growth: Lessons from Microeconomic Evidence, in New Developments in Productivity Analysis
Foster, Haltiwanger and Syverson, 2008: Reallocation, Firm Turnover, and Efficiency: Selection on Productivity or Profitability?, American Economic Review
Davis, Haltiwanger and Schuh, 1996: Job Creation and Destruction, MIT Press
Syverson, 2011: What Determines Productivity?, Journal of Economic Literature

candidates.reasoning: Using administrative microdata, this work showed how aggregate productivity and employment emerge from entry, exit and reallocation across heterogeneous establishments. The reservation is that it is a cumulative, measurement-based programme with diffuse credit and hard causal identification.
candidates.grouping_note: Joins job-flow nominations (with Steven J. Davis) and productivity-dispersion nominations (with Syverson); Davis and Chang-Tai Hsieh are left out of the lineup.

candidates.motivation: for the empirical analysis of entry and competition in concentrated markets

defining_works.work: Bresnahan and Reiss, 1991: Entry and Competition in Concentrated Markets, Journal of Political Economy
Bresnahan and Reiss, 1990: Entry in Monopoly Markets, Review of Economic Studies

candidates.reasoning: Bresnahan and Reiss gave a transparent identification strategy inferring competitive conduct from entry and market size, replicated across many industries. Its impact is seen as narrower than BLP and the joint nominations as less unified.
candidates.grouping_note: n025, n037 and n093 also name John Sutton, who has his own candidate and is left out of this lineup; n037 also cites Bresnahan 1982, which anchors the separate NEIO candidate.

candidates.motivation: for the economic analysis of regulation and restructuring in network industries, especially electricity

defining_works.work: Joskow and Schmalensee, 1983: Markets for Power, MIT Press
Joskow, 1997: "Restructuring, Competition and Regulatory Reform in the U.S. Electricity Sector", Journal of Economic Perspectives
Joskow and Rose, 1989: "The Effects of Economic Regulation", in Handbook of Industrial Organization

candidates.reasoning: Their work shaped electricity-market restructuring and is highly relevant to decarbonization policy. Reservations are that the contribution is applied and less sharply delineated, and overlaps with Tirole's 2014 prize.
candidates.grouping_note: Lineups vary between Joskow alone, Joskow-Schmalensee and Joskow-Rose-Borenstein; Severin Borenstein is left out.

candidates.motivation: for the analysis of network effects, compatibility and standards

people_others.name: Hal R. Varian
people_others.affiliation: Google and University of California, Berkeley

defining_works.work: Katz and Shapiro, 1985: Network Externalities, Competition, and Compatibility, American Economic Review
Katz and Shapiro, 1986: Technology Adoption in the Presence of Network Externalities, Journal of Political Economy

candidates.reasoning: This work is foundational for technology adoption, standards competition and digital-market policy. Reservations are shared credit with Farrell and Saloner and closeness to platform economics and Tirole's prize.
candidates.grouping_note: Joseph Farrell (n049) and Hal R. Varian (n059) are each named once and left out of the lineup.

candidates.motivation: for the theoretical analysis of exclusionary practices, collusion and antitrust policy

defining_works.work: Whinston, 1990: Tying, Foreclosure, and Exclusion, American Economic Review
Bernheim and Whinston, 1990: Multimarket Contact and Collusive Behavior, RAND Journal of Economics
Bernheim and Whinston, 1986: Menu Auctions, Resource Allocation, and Economic Influence, Quarterly Journal of Economics

candidates.reasoning: Whinston's game-theoretic models of tying, exclusion and multimarket collusion are said to shape antitrust standards. The reservation is that the contribution is dispersed across topics and largely theoretical.
candidates.grouping_note: Most nominations name Whinston alone; Bernheim appears only in n005.
flags: resembles an awarded motivation: 2014 Jean Tirole: "for his analysis of market power and regulation" [L51] (word overlap 0.40)

candidates.motivation: for models of firm selection, entry, exit and industry dynamics

defining_works.work: Hopenhayn, 1992: Entry, Exit, and Firm Dynamics in Long Run Equilibrium, Econometrica
Jovanovic, 1982: Selection and the Evolution of Industry, Econometrica

candidates.reasoning: These canonical models of learning, selection, entry and exit underpin the analysis of productivity dispersion and are central to quantitative macro and IO. The reservation is that their influence is embedded in later empirical and computational literatures.
candidates.grouping_note: n078 also names Ericson and Pakes, whose dynamic oligopoly framework forms a separate candidate; they are left out here.

candidates.motivation: for founding the new empirical industrial organization and the identification of market power

defining_works.work: Bresnahan, 1982: The Oligopoly Solution Concept is Identified, Economics Letters
Porter, 1983: A Study of Cartel Stability: The Joint Executive Committee, 1880-1886, Bell Journal of Economics

candidates.reasoning: These nominations credit Bresnahan with showing how market power and conduct can be identified without cost data, laying the groundwork for modern structural IO. No major reservation is raised.
candidates.grouping_note: Porter appears only in n112 and is also in the separate Green-Porter collusion candidate.

candidates.motivation: for the analysis of relational contracts and incentives inside organizations

defining_works.work: Baker, Gibbons and Murphy, 2002: Relational Contracts and the Theory of the Firm, Quarterly Journal of Economics
Baker, Gibbons and Murphy, 1994: Subjective Performance Measures in Optimal Incentive Contracts, Quarterly Journal of Economics
Gibbons, 2005: Four Formal(izable) Theories of the Firm?, Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization

candidates.reasoning: This work makes informal incentives and repeated relationships central to firm governance and boundaries. The reservation is its proximity to contract theory and the Holmström and Williamson prizes.
candidates.grouping_note: Two nominations name Gibbons alone; the others name the Baker-Gibbons-Murphy team.

candidates.motivation: for methods to estimate production functions and productivity from firm-level data

defining_works.work: Olley and Pakes, 1996: The Dynamics of Productivity in the Telecommunications Equipment Industry, Econometrica
Levinsohn and Petrin, 2003: "Estimating Production Functions Using Inputs to Control for Unobservables", Review of Economic Studies

candidates.reasoning: These methods underpin micro-founded productivity measurement, reallocation accounting and policy evaluation with plant-level data. The reservation is that credit is diffuse and overlaps with the BLP case.
candidates.grouping_note: Joins the Olley-Pakes nomination with the Pakes-Levinsohn-Petrin one; Amil Petrin is left out of the lineup on a tie with Levinsohn.

candidates.motivation: for the empirical analysis of contracting and organizational form, notably franchising

defining_works.work: Lafontaine, 1992: Agency Theory and Franchising: Some Empirical Results, RAND Journal of Economics
Lafontaine and Slade, 2007: Retail Contracting, AER

candidates.reasoning: She tests contracting theory with detailed franchise-contract data, opening the black box of organizational rules. No major reservation is raised.
candidates.grouping_note: n154 also names Kathryn Shaw, who has a separate personnel-economics candidate and is left out here.

candidates.motivation: for contributions to the industrial organization of platform markets, market design and machine learning in IO

defining_works.work: Athey, S., & Ellison, G., 2011: Position Auctions with Consumer Search, Quarterly Journal of Economics
Athey & Imbens, 2016: Recursive partitioning for heterogeneous causal effects, PNAS

candidates.reasoning: Athey is credited with joining mechanism design and empirical IO in platform markets and improving causal inference in large datasets. The focus is mostly on modern digital economies.
candidates.grouping_note: Joins two Athey nominations that stress platforms and machine learning respectively.

candidates.motivation: for the theory of dynamic capabilities and the strategic management of the firm

defining_works.work: Teece, Pisano, and Shuen, 1997: Dynamic capabilities and strategic management, Strategic Management Journal

candidates.reasoning: Teece's dynamic capabilities explain how firms innovate and adapt to technological change. The framework is conceptual and hard to formalize or test at scale.
candidates.grouping_note: Three nominations with the same person and work.

candidates.motivation: for making dynamic industry equilibrium and forward-looking firm decisions empirically tractable

defining_works.work: Ericson and Pakes, 1995: Markov-Perfect Industry Dynamics: A Framework for Empirical Work, Review of Economic Studies
Rust, 1987: "Optimal Replacement of GMC Bus Engines: An Empirical Model of Harold Zurcher", Econometrica
Pakes and McGuire, 1994: Computing Markov-Perfect Nash Equilibria: Numerical Implications of a Dynamic Differentiated Product Model, RAND Journal of Economics

candidates.reasoning: The work made investment, entry, exit and dynamic strategic conduct estimable and computable, enabling policy counterfactuals. Reservations are computational demands, model dependence and overlap with the BLP nomination through Pakes.
candidates.grouping_note: Joins two dynamic structural IO nominations with different co-nominees; Patrick Bajari is left out of the lineup.

candidates.motivation: for the comparative analysis of legal origins and the economic consequences of regulation

defining_works.work: La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer, & Vishny, 1998: Law and Finance, Journal of Political Economy
Djankov, La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, & Shleifer, 2002: The Regulation of Entry, Quarterly Journal of Economics

candidates.reasoning: Their large data collection on entry regulation and legal systems is highly influential across political economy. The exogeneity of legal origins is heavily contested.

candidates.motivation: for the empirical analysis of media markets and the use of text as data

defining_works.work: Gentzkow and Shapiro, 2010: What Drives Media Slant? Evidence from U.S. Daily Newspapers, Econometrica

candidates.reasoning: The work pioneers transparent measurement of media slant with large text datasets and sets a high reproducibility standard. No reservation is raised.

candidates.motivation: for the theory and empirical analysis of collusion under imperfect monitoring

defining_works.work: Green and Porter, 1984: Noncooperative Collusion under Imperfect Price Information, Econometrica
Porter, 1983: A Study of Cartel Stability: The Joint Executive Committee, 1880-1886, Bell Journal of Economics

candidates.reasoning: The work links repeated-game theory of price wars to a falsifiable empirical test that informs antitrust. Its scope is narrow and the evidence rests on a single historical cartel.
candidates.grouping_note: Two identical-lineup nominations; Porter also appears in the NEIO candidate with Bresnahan.

candidates.motivation: for structural demand estimation using granular scanner data

defining_works.work: Nevo, 2001: Measuring Market Power in the Ready-to-Eat Cereal Industry, Econometrica

candidates.reasoning: Nevo showed how to apply structural demand estimation to large scanner datasets to measure market power. Robustness to specification choices remains a question.

candidates.motivation: for empirical models of selection and imperfect competition in insurance markets

defining_works.work: Einav, Finkelstein, and Cullen, 2010: Estimating Welfare in Insurance Markets Using Variation in Prices, Quarterly Journal of Economics

candidates.reasoning: They imported structural IO tools into public finance to identify adverse selection and moral hazard. No reservation is raised.

candidates.motivation: for the economic theory of regulation and interest-group influence on regulators

defining_works.work: Peltzman, 1976: Toward a More General Theory of Regulation, Journal of Law and Economics
Peltzman, 1975: The Effects of Automobile Safety Regulation, Journal of Political Economy

candidates.reasoning: This work treats regulators as political institutions shaped by interest groups. It is close to Stigler's 1982 prize.

candidates.motivation: for the analysis of consumer search, price dispersion and obfuscation in retail markets

defining_works.work: Varian, 1980: A Model of Sales, American Economic Review
Ellison and Ellison, 2009: Search, Obfuscation, and Price Elasticities on the Internet, Econometrica

candidates.reasoning: The work is central to understanding price dispersion and e-commerce. Foundations are partly Diamond's and the pairing is less canonical.

candidates.motivation: for the theory of contestable markets and industry cost structure

defining_works.work: Baumol, Panzar and Willig, 1982: Contestable Markets and the Theory of Industry Structure, Harcourt Brace Jovanovich

candidates.reasoning: The theory shaped regulatory thinking on natural monopoly and multiproduct costs. Its empirical relevance is contested and Baumol is deceased.

candidates.motivation: for the empirical analysis of human resource management and insider econometrics

defining_works.work: Ichniowski, Shaw, and Prennushi, 1997: The Effects of Human Resource Management Practices on Productivity: A Study of Steel Finishing Lines, American Economic Review

candidates.reasoning: Shaw uses detailed plant-level data to analyze incentive structures and productivity. No reservation is raised.

candidates.motivation: for contributions to contract theory and the theory of the firm

defining_works.work: Bolton, P., & Dewatripont, M., 2005: Contract Theory, MIT Press

candidates.reasoning: Their synthesis of contract theory maps incentive constraints within hierarchies with outstanding clarity. Contract theory belongs mainly to another field.

candidates.motivation: for the empirical measurement of markups and market power from production data

defining_works.work: De Loecker and Warzynski, 2012: Markups and Firm-Level Export Status, American Economic Review
De Loecker, Eeckhout and Unger, 2020: The Rise of Market Power and the Macroeconomic Implications, Quarterly Journal of Economics

candidates.reasoning: The work reopened markup measurement and linked IO to macro concerns about concentration. Estimates are sensitive to production-function assumptions and are under active robustness debate.
